claim: Copper plates dated 758 and 768 AD are the earliest references to the Pune region and record Rashtrakuta rule, naming the place Punaka/Punya Vishaya.

sources.quote: Evidence found as copper plates of 758 AD and of 768 AD reveal that the Rashtrakootas ruled this region at that time.
The first reference to Pune region is found in two copper plates dated to 758 and 768 AD, issued by Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I.
The copper plates of 758 and 768 CE show that the Yadava dynasty had renamed the city as Punakavishaya and Punya Vishaya.

claim: After the Rashtrakutas, the region was ruled by the Yadava dynasty of Devagiri, which held Pune until 1327.

sources.quote: Pune was part of the territory ruled by the Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri from the 9th century to 1327.
Pune was ruled by the Yadava dynasty after the Rashtrakootas.

claim: The name Pune is explained in the Pune Gazetteer as 'Punya', meaning a holy place.

sources.quote: The Pune Gazetteer explains the term Pune as Punya - a holy place.
'Vishaya' means land, while 'Punaka' and 'Punya' mean holy.

claim: Shivaji grew up at Lal Mahal with his mother Jijabai, in a palace built by his father Shahaji in the razed city of Pune.

sources.quote: Pune became popular with the rise of Maratha ruler Shivaji. He spent his early childhood in Pune at Lal Mahal, a palace built by his father Shahaji, where Shivaji's mother Jijabai lived for a decade.
Young Shivaji grew up here, and stayed in the Lal Mahal with his mother Jijabai till he captured the Torna fort in 1645.

claim: Tanaji Malusare fell recapturing the Kondhana fort in 1670, after which Shivaji renamed it Sinhagad — the Lion's Fort.

sources.quote: In 1670, Shivaji reconquered the fort for the third time through his Koli Subedar, Tanaji Malusare in Battle of Sinhagad, and the fort came and stayed under Maratha rule till 1689 A.D.

Restoration workers at Sinhagad Fort, 35 km from Pune, have stumbled upon the original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare, the brave Maratha warrior after whom Shivaji is said to have named Sinhagad Fort (Lion's fort). Malusare died in 1670 after being seriously wounded in the Sinhagad battle.
It has a strong historical significance because Maratha warrior Tanhaji fought and died here in the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.

claim: Sinhagad, formerly Kondhana, is the most prominent fort near Pune, about 25 km from the city on a hill some 1,290 m high.

sources.quote: Sinhagad, ealier known as ‘Kondhana’ is the most prominent and popular fort in Pune.It is located at village Donaje, taluka-Haveli. It is 25 km away from Pune on a hill 1290 m high.

Sinhagad (also known as the Lion's Fort) is an ancient hill fortress located at around 28 kilometres southwest of Pune, India. Previously known as Kondhana, the fort has been the site of many battles, most notably the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.

claim: Restoration workers at Sinhagad uncovered the original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare, buried under concrete and layers of paint.

sources.quote: The original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare was unearthed by the restoration workers in February 2019.
The stone structure, found buried under cement, concrete, and layers of oil paint, is believed to be around 350 years old.

claim: Nanasaheb Peshwa (Balaji Bajirav), the third Peshwa, ruled from 1740 to 1761 and expanded Peshwa administration over Poona.

sources.quote: Nanasaheb Peshwa succeeded Thorala Bajirao Peshwa and ruled the Maratha kingdom from 1740 to 1761.
Balaji Bajirav, alias Nanasaheb, Third Peshwa, 1740-1761.

claim: The College of Engineering Pune (now COEP Technological University) was chartered in 1854 and is the third oldest engineering college in Asia.

sources.quote: College of Engineering, Pune (CoEP), chartered in 1854 is a nationally respected leader in technical education.
COEP’s precursor, The Poona Engineering Class and Mechanical School was opened in July 1854, with an aim to provide suitable learning to the subordinate officers in the Public Works Department.
The College of Engineering Pune, an autonomous institute of the government of Maharashtra founded in 1854, is the third oldest engineering college in Asia.

claim: Pune is known as the 'Oxford of the East' because of its concentration of educational institutions.

sources.quote: Pune also has made its mark as the educational epicenter winning itself the sobriquet, 'The Oxford of the East'.
Surrounded with green hills and placid lakes and having a salubrious climate, Pune is known as the Queen of the Deccan and Oxford of the East.
Pune is often referred to as the "Oxford of the East" because of its educational institutions.

claim: Chakan, Talegaon and Pimpri-Chinchwad form the industrial belt of the Pune region.

sources.quote: Hinjawadi is well-connected to the suburbs of Baner and Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan and Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Hinjawadi is in proximity to the suburbs of Baner near Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan, and Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Major industrial areas around Pune are Chakan, Chinchwad, Bhosari, Pirangut, Hinjawadi, Talegaon, Talawade, Urse.

claim: Pimpri-Chinchwad is called the most rapidly developing city in Asia and the third fastest growing city in the country, with a vast network of industrial establishments.

sources.quote: Pimpri-Chinchwad, since its establishment 50 years ago, has grown rapidly. It is often called the most rapidly developing city in Asia. Industry-wise, no other city in Maharashtra has such a vast network of establishments.
In the last two decades, Pimpri Chinchwad is the third fastest growing city in the country.
It is one of the most rapidly developing suburban areas in India and has emerged as the third fastest growing city in the country.

claim: Bajaj Auto, the Pune-headquartered two- and three-wheeler manufacturer, runs science-and-technology skill development programmes for youth.

sources.quote: Bajaj Auto, headquartered in Pune, is ranked as the world's fourth largest two and three wheeler manufacturer.
Bajaj Auto is committed to promoting science and technology as part of its CSR focus areas i.e. Skill-development in STEM.

claim: The Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjawadi spreads over about 2,800 acres and houses offices of over 800 companies.

sources.quote: It houses the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, a large tech and business park spread over 2,800 acres, which was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation. The business park has offices of over 800 companies.

After Bengaluru, the reverberations of downsizing are being felt acutely across the 2,800-acre Hinjewadi IT Park, which houses all the big guns: Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant, IBM and Tech Mahindra, among others.

claim: The Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjawadi was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation at a cost of Rs 155 crore.

sources.quote: Built at a cost of Rs 155 crore by MIDC, the IT park is challenged by chaotic traffic, insufficient security arrangements and shortage of power supply among many other things.
It houses the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, a large tech and business park spread over 2,800 acres, which was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation.

claim: Hinjawadi is popularly known as Pune's Silicon Valley and is the anchor of the western Indian IT industry.

sources.quote: Popularly known as Pune’s Silicon Valley, Hinjawadi has the presence of top multinationals.
It has made this region the Silicon Valley of western India.
Hinjawadi (also incorrectly spelt Hinjewadi and Henjewadi) is a suburb in Pune, India.

claim: Ganeshotsav is Pune's premier festival, with the Dagadusheth Ganapati among the city's most honoured Ganpatis, a public form given to the festival by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

sources.quote: Years later, when Lokmanya Tilak started the practice of organising annual Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in Maharashtra, Dagdusheth Ganpati gained fame as the most adored deity in Pune.

Ganesh Chaturthi is widely and publicly celebrated in Pune. Lokamanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak started the public celebration of the festival as a means to circumvent the colonial British government ban on Hindu gatherings through its anti-public assembly legislation in 1892.

It is the most popular among the thousands of deities that are housed in the lanes and bylanes of Pune city, including the big five Ganpatis that are considered of high honour during the annual festival.

claim: The Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati temple, in Pune's Budhwar Peth, was founded after the halwai couple lost their son in a plague epidemic and is visited by over a hundred thousand devotees a year.

sources.quote: The story dates back to more than 125 years when Shri Dagdusheth Halwai and his wife Lakshmibai lived in Pune. As fate would have it, they lost their only son to the plague epidemic.
The temple is visited by over one hundred thousand devotees every year.
The Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati holds the rare distinction of being named after a devotee, its inceptor; but it wasn’t always called so.

claim: Ganeshotsav is the most important and biggest festival of Pune, falling in the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada, with public pandals holding idols for five to ten days.

sources.quote: This is the most important and biggest festival in Pune. It falls on the 4th day of the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada (August - September). People buy Ganesh images to keep in their houses as a divine guest for five to ten days.
Ganesh Chaturthi is widely and publicly celebrated in Pune.

claim: Pune is the cultural capital of Maharashtra, a centre for Marathi theatre, music, literature and education.

sources.quote: Pune, the cultural capital of Maharashtra, is an important city of India.
The city leads as the 'veritable heartland' of cultural Maharashtra.

Pune has historically been a major cultural centre, with important figures like Dnyaneshwar, Shivaji, Tukaram, Baji Rao I, Balaji Baji Rao, Madhavrao I, Nana Fadnavis, Mahadev Govind Ranade, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Mahatma Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Tarabai Shinde, Dhondo Keshav Karve, and Pandita Ramabai doing their life's work in Pune City or in an area that falls in Pune Metropolitan Region.

claim: Pune is the largest city in Maharashtra by area, with a geographical area of 516.18 square kilometres.

sources.quote: In terms of the total amount of land under its jurisdiction, Pune is the largest city in Maharashtra by area, with a geographical area of 516.18km2, though by population it comes in a distant second to Mumbai.
With its new urban city limits, Pune has now become the seventh largest city in India, with the geographical area of 516.18 sq km (from 331 sq km).

claim: The old city of Pune stands at the confluence (the Sangam) of the Mula and Mutha rivers.

sources.quote: The old city of Pune is at the confluence of the Mula and Mutha rivers.

There is a rather good old-time coloured picture in the Western India Club by Henry Salt, showing the Sangam, or junction of the Miitha and Mula rivers, the City, and the Parbatti hill beyond, and the old-time Residency with the white flag and the red cross of St. George floating over it in the year 1809.

claim: The Panshet dam burst on 12 July 1961, causing massive flooding in Pune and killing nearly 1,000 people.

sources.quote: The Panshet Dam burst on 12 July 1961, during its first year of storing water. The failure occurred when the dam wall gave way due to the complete lack of reinforced cement concrete (RCC) reinforcement in the conduit passing through the earthen structure. Instead of using RCC, plain unreinforced concrete blocks were installed, owing to a shortage of steel at the time. This critical design compromise led to a catastrophic failure, resulting in massive flooding in Pune and an estimated death toll of around 1,000 people.

The fateful day of July 12, 1961, brings forward dark memories of the Panshet flood that killed nearly 1,000 people in Pune. On this day, the under-construction Panshet dam breached in the early hours, leading to massive floods in Pune and surrounding areas.

claim: The 1961 dam-burst flood left Pune's low-lying old city submerged and put all bridges under water except the Bund Garden Bridge.

sources.quote: The low-lying areas of the old city were almost completely submerged. Except for the rail bridge of the Sangam Bridges, two adjacent bridges built separately for rail and road traffic and Bund Garden Bridge, all other bridges were under water as well.

The havoc forced people to flee to places as high as Parvati hills as the low lying areas of the city were almost completely submerged. Except for the Bund Garden Bridge, all bridges were under water as well.

claim: Khadakwasla Lake, formed by the dam on the Mutha River, is the main source of water for Pune and its suburbs, and drinking water is piped from Khadakwasla to the city.

sources.quote: Khadakwasla Dam is a dam on the Mutha River 21 km (13 mi) from the centre of the city of Pune in Maharashtra, India. The dam created a reservoir known as Khadakwasla Lake which is the main source of water for Pune and its suburbs.
The civic administration has introduced a pipeline to fetch drinking water from Khadakwasla up to the city.

claim: Rising pollution in the Mula-Mutha river has reduced the number of migratory birds that come to the village of Kavadi in Pune district.

sources.quote: The river flows through the village of Kavadi in the Pune district, witnesses many migratory birds. However, increase in pollution in the recent years has resulted in a reduction in the number of birds.
However, rising pollution in the Mula-Mutha that flows through the village has led to a fall in the number of birds coming to Kavadi with each passing year.

claim: The Mula-Mutha river flows through the village of Kavadi in Pune district.

sources.quote: The river flows through the village of Kavadi in the Pune district, witnesses many migratory birds.
However, rising pollution in the Mula-Mutha that flows through the village has led to a fall in the number of birds coming to Kavadi with each passing year.

claim: Sinhagad (Singarh) fort is a cliff-top stronghold of the Sahyadri range, captured by Tanaji Malusare from the Mughals, that looms above the Khadakwasla complex.

sources.quote: Perched on an isolated cliff of the Bhuleswar range in the Sahyadri Mountains, the fort is situated on a hill about 760 metres (2,490 ft) above ground and 1,317 metres (4,321 ft) above mean sea level.

The Khadakwasla complex is dominated by the looming blue skyline of the Sinhgarh Fort Complex It looms over the Academy like a colossus, an overpowering iconic presence. Situated atop this blue massif is the famous Singarh fort which Tanaji Mlusare, the favorite General of Shivaji, had captured from the Moghuls in a daring and incredible assault up a cliff face.

claim: The Battle of Khadki, also called the Battle of Kirkee or Ganeshkhind, was fought on 5 November 1817 between the British East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy.

sources.quote: The Battle of Khadki, also known as or the Battle of Ganeshkhind and Battle of Kirkee, took place at modern day Khadki, India, on 5 November 1817 between the forces of the British East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy under the leadership of Appasaheb Bhonsle.
From here we get an extended view of the field of action of November 5, 1817, which practically settled the Peishwa and the Maharattas finally in this part of India.

claim: The Battle of Koregaon was fought on 1 January 1818 at Koregaon Bhima, where a small East India Company force faced the Peshwa's army.

sources.quote: The Battle of Koregaon was fought on 1 January 1818 between the East India Company and the Peshwa faction of the Maratha Empire, at Koregaon Bhima. A 28,000-strong force led by Peshwa Baji Rao II whilst on their way to attack the company-held Pune, were unexpectedly met by an 800-strong Company force that was on its way to reinforce the British troops in Pune.

On reaching the high ground above the village of Koregaon, about ten in the morning of the first of January 1818, the battalion saw the Peshwa's army of 25,000 Maratha horse on the eastern bank of the Bhima.

claim: The Mahatma Phule Mandai (Lord Reay Market) in Pune was built by the municipality between 1882 and 1886 and inaugurated by the Governor of Bombay, Lord Reay, also serving as the municipal office.

sources.quote: In the early years of the British rule, an open-air vegetable market used to be held outside the Shaniwar Wada. This shifted to an indoor place built by the Poona Municipality, which was inaugurated in 1886. The market was named after the then Governor of Bombay, Lord Reay, and served as retail and wholesale market in addition to being the municipal office.

The construction of the building began in 1882, and was completed in 1886. A total of Rs 2.30 lakhs was spent on the construction. It was inaugurated at the hands of the then governor of Bombay, Lord Reay, after whom the mandai was named as Lord Reay market.

claim: In 1818 the Peshwas were dethroned and the British established a permanent army cantonment in Pune, with cantonments in the eastern part of the city and at nearby Khadki.

sources.quote: In 1818 the Peshwas were dethroned and the British established a permanent Army Cantonment.

After the fall of Peshwa rule in 1818, the British East India Company made the city one of its major military bases. They established military cantonments in the eastern part of the city, and another one at nearby Khadki.

claim: Southern Command, the oldest command of the Indian Army, was established on 1 April 1895 and is headquartered in Pune.

sources.quote: The Southern Command of the Indian Army, established in 1895, is headquartered in Pune cantonment.

The southern command, which is the oldest command of the Indian Army, was established on April 1, 1895. The command, which has its headquarters in Pune, is responsible for conducting military operations over nearly 41 per cent of Indian landmass covering 10 states and four union territories.

claim: The city's name was changed from the British-era English name 'Poona' to 'Pune' in 1978.

sources.quote: Anglicized to Poona in 1857 by the English during British rule, the city's name was changed to Pune in 1978.
Britishers named the city Poona, but it was replaced with a more traditional ‘Pune’ in 1978.

claim: Peshwa rule ended with the defeat of Peshwa Baji Rao II by the British East India Company in 1818, after which the British established the administration of the region.

sources.quote: The Peshwa rule ended with the defeat of Peshwa Bajirao II by the British East India Company in 1818.
British defeated the Marathas in 1818 and established the administration in this region.

claim: During the Third Anglo-Maratha War, East India Company General Pritzler besieged Sinhagad fort and it passed into British hands.

sources.quote: During the Third Anglo-Maratha War in 1817, the East India Company General Pritzler laid siege to the fort on the orders of Mountstuart Elphinstone, the company resident in Pune, and it passed into the British hands.

On the 14th of February Brigadier General Pritzler marched from Satara by the Nira bridge to Sinhgad. The siege was begun on the 24th of February and on the 2nd of March, after 1417 shells and 2281 shot had been spent, the garrison of 700 Gosavis and 400 Arabs hold out a white flag and next day surrendered the fort.

claim: Mahatma Gandhi, Kasturba Gandhi and Mahadev Desai were imprisoned at the Aga Khan Palace in Pune during the Quit India Movement, where Kasturba Gandhi and Mahadev Desai died.

sources.quote: Mahatma Gandhi, his wife Kasturba Gandhi and his secretary Mahadev Desai were interned in the palace from 9 August 1942 to 6 May 1944, following the launch of Quit India Movement. Kasturba Gandhi and Mahadev Desai died during their captivity period in the palace and have their Samadhis located over there.

The palace itself is a majestic building and considered amongst the greatest of the architectural marvels of India. The place is so closely linked with the country’s freedom movement, as this is where Mahatma and Kasturba Gandhi, his secretary Mahadev Desai and Sarojini Naidu were incarcerated and where Kasturba Gandhi and Mahadev Desai breathed their last.

claim: The Pune-Mumbai rail track was constructed by the British in the 1850s and was operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway.

sources.quote: A railway line from Bombay, which was operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR), reached the city in 1858.
The Pune-Mumbai rail track and the Khadakwasla Dam were constructed in 1857.

claim: Poona became the capital of the Maratha Empire under the Peshwas, with the Shanwar Wada as the centre of Maratha government.

sources.quote: Balaji left the Raja in Raghuji's charge and went to Poona, and from this time Poona became the capital of the Maratha empire.

He assumed the entire administration of the kingdom himself and moved the capital from Satara to Poona. For sixty-eight years the Shanwar Wada or Saturday Palace, begun by Bajirao, finished by Balaji and added to by his successors, became the centre of the Maratha Government. As the Maratha power overshadowed that of Delhi, Poona became the real capital of India.

claim: Peshwa Bajirao I laid the ceremonial foundation of Shaniwar Wada on 10 January 1730.

sources.quote: Peshwa Baji Rao I, prime minister to Chattrapati Shahu, laid the ceremonial foundation of his own residence on Saturday, 10 January 1730. It was named Shaniwar Wada from the Marathi words Shaniwar (Saturday) and Wada (a general term for any residence complex). Teak was imported from the jungles of Junnar, stone was brought from the nearby quarries of Chinchwad, and Lime (mineral) was brought from the lime-belts of Jejuri. Shaniwarwada was completed in 1732, at a total cost of Rs. 16,110, a very large sum at that time. The opening ceremony was performed according to religious customs, on 22 January 1732, another Saturday chosen for being a particularly auspicious day.
The foundation stone of the building was laid by Bajirao I (1720-1740) on Saturday, the 10th of January 1730, being an auspicious day.

claim: The total expenditure incurred on building Shaniwar Wada came up to Rs. 16,110.

sources.quote: Shaniwarwada was completed in 1732, at a total cost of Rs. 16,110, a very large sum at that time.
It is stated that the total expenditure incurred on this Palace came up to Rs. 16,110.

claim: Peshwa Nanasaheb built the Parvati temple complex on Parvati Hill together with the Heera Baug garden and its lake.

sources.quote: On the southern fringe of the city, Nanasaheb built a palace on the Parvati Hill. In the vicinity of the hill, he developed a garden called Heera Baug and dug a lake with a Ganesh temple on an island in the middle of the lake.
Nanasaheb Peshwa constructed Parvati Temple complex, which is known to be the pride of the Pune city.

claim: A great fire broke out inside the Shaniwar Wada palace complex in 1828 and the conflagration raged for seven days, destroying most of the palace.

sources.quote: On 27 February 1828, a great fire started inside the palace complex. The conflagration raged for seven days.
The construction of the Shaniwarwada was completed on January 22, 1732, two years after Peshwa Bajirao began its conception. Most of it was reduced to ashes during a fire in 1828.

claim: Shahaji entrusted his fief of Poona and Supa to his wife Jijabai, leaving his younger son Shivaji with her at Poona.

sources.quote: When Maloji's son, Shahaji had to join campaigns in distant southern India for the Adil Shahi sultanate, he selected Pune for the residence of his wife, Jijabai and younger son, Shivaji (1630-1680), the future founder of the Maratha Empire.

He took service with the Bijapur kingdom and took with him his eldest son Sambhaji, leaving behind him his wife Jijabai and her younger son Shivaji. To provide for her maintenance Shahaji entrusted to her his fief of Poona and Supa.

claim: Shivaji defeated Shaista Khan, Aurangzeb's uncle, at Lal Mahal in Pune.

sources.quote: It was at Poona that Shivaji made his daring raid on Shaistekhan's house.
Aurangazeb's uncle, Shahistekhan was defeated at Lal Mahal by Shivaji.

claim: Mughal emperor Aurangzeb renamed Pune as Muhiyabad.

sources.quote: Mughal emperor Aurangzeb renamed a small neighbourhood in central part of the old city as Muhiyabad (the only divergent naming) some time between 1703 and 1705 in memory of his great-grandson Muhi-ul-Milan, who died there. The name Muhiyabad was reverted soon after Aurangzeb's death.
Aurangazeb named Pune as Muhiyabad after the death of Shivaji in 1680.

claim: Savitribai Phule Pune University, formerly the University of Poona, was established on 10 February 1949 under the Poona University Act.

sources.quote: The Savitribai Phule Pune University (formerly known as University of Poona) was established on 10th February 1949 under the Poona University Act, passed by the Bombay Legislature in 1948.

The education sector in the city continued its growth in the post-independence era with the establishment of the University of Pune (now, Savitribai Phule Pune University) in 1949, the National Chemical Laboratory in 1950 and the National Defence Academy in 1955.

claim: The National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla in Pune was formally inaugurated on 16 January 1955.

sources.quote: On 07 December 1954, the interim process crystallized with the commissioning of the National Defence Academy. Formal inauguration of the Academy took place on 16 January 1955.

The education sector in the city continued its growth in the post-independence era with the establishment of the University of Pune (now, Savitribai Phule Pune University) in 1949, the National Chemical Laboratory in 1950 and the National Defence Academy in 1955.

claim: Fergusson College was set up in Pune in 1885 by the Deccan Education Society, with founders including Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar.

sources.quote: It was founded in 1885 by Vaman Shriram Apte, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Vishnushashtri Chiplunkar, Mahadeo Ballal Namjoshi and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar.
The Deccan Education Societyâ€™s Fergusson College, set up in Pune in 1885 by stalwarts such as Lokmanya Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, will be converted into a state university.

claim: Deccan College began as a Hindu college teaching Sanskrit set up by the Company government, and it led the educational movement in British-era Pune.

sources.quote: In the 1820s, the company government set up a Hindu college, to impart education in Sanskrit. In the 1840s, the college started offering a more contemporary curriculum. The college was then renamed as Poona College, and later Deccan College.
Pune has been recognized as a seat of learning and the Deccan College (1851) led the educational movement in Pune.

claim: Pune has 3.62 million registered vehicles, more than its population.

sources.quote: According to reports published in April 2018, the number of vehicles registered in the city stands at 3.62 million surpassing the population of the city.

While the population stands at approximately 3.5 million (35 lakh), the number of registered vehicles for the area is now 3.62 million (36.2 lakh) under the Regional Traffic Office MH-12, said RTO chief Babasahen Ajri.

claim: Pune has become a nerve centre for automobiles and is one of the most important automobile and manufacturing hubs of India.

sources.quote: It is also one of the most important automobile and manufacturing hubs of India.
It has also become the nerve center for IT-BT, automobiles and real estate among other things.

claim: Pune's Hinjawadi-Shivajinagar metro line is being executed by the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority as a public-private partnership.

sources.quote: Line 3 Puneri Metro is being implemented by Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) and is a joint venture of Tata Projects and Siemens Pune IT City Metro Rail Limited on a public–private partnership basis.

PUNE: The state cabinet on Tuesday gave its nod to the 23.3km Hinjawadi-Shivajinagar Metro line, which will be built at a cost of Rs 8,313 crore and executed by the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA).

claim: Construction of the Magarpatta township in Pune began in 2000 with a residential block of 72 apartments.

sources.quote: Construction began in 2000 and continues as of 2025.
We started construction in March 2000 with a residential block of 72 apartments.

claim: Tulshi Baug is an old, noisy and unorganised market area of Pune with temporary stalls and lined shops.

sources.quote: There was also an older market-district called Tulshi Baug, close to the vegetable market that sold a variety of household items.
Tulsi Baug is a noisy and unorganized market area with temporary stalls and lined shops.

claim: The Osho ashram, also called the Osho Communal Centre, is located at Koregaon Park in Pune.

sources.quote: The Osho International Meditation Resort, one of the world's largest spiritual centres, is located in Koregaon Park and attracts visitors from over a hundred countries.
Osho Ashram, also known as the Osho Communal Centre is located at the greenery area of 17 Koregoan Park of the city.

claim: Clashes erupted in Pune during the 200th anniversary commemoration of the Bhima-Koregaon battle.

sources.quote: On 1 January 2018, clashes erupted between Hindu groups and Dalit Buddhist groups during the commemoration of this battle.
Clashes between Dalit groups and supporters of right-wing Hindu organisations during the 200th anniversary celebrations of the Bhima-Koregaon battle in Pune district had left a man dead on Monday.
